Why Sandro Tonali is out for Tottenham against Ipswich as Roberto De Zerbi offers explanation

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 14:40, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 14:53.
  • Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed that Sandro Tonali is missing from Saturday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town due to illness.
  • The Italy international was a surprise absentee from the Lilywhites' squad against the Tractor Boys, as Conor Gallagher was instead given the nod in central midfield with Mateus Fernandes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 14:40, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 14:53.

Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed that Sandro Tonali is missing from Saturday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town due to illness.

The Italy international was a surprise absentee from the Lilywhites' squad against the Tractor Boys, as Conor Gallagher was instead given the nod in central midfield with Mateus Fernandes.

Tonali was not name-checked in De Zerbi's pre-game press conference, and the expectation was that the former Newcastle United man would make his 11th Premier League start of the season.

However, Tonali's perfect starting streak in the top-flight campaign is now over, and De Zerbi explained the midfielder's absence when speaking to reporters ahead of kickoff.

"(The reasons for the changes are) a combination of physical condition (and defeat to Leeds). Many players, they came back (from international duty) not in the right condition. (Sandro) Tonali was sick for a couple of days. Rodrigo Bentancur arrived yesterday, just yesterday working with us," De Zerbi said.

In a recent development, "I am lucky because I have a great squad. Many players. All players are very close in level so now we start a very tough period of three games in a row. We are ready.".

De Zerbi made a total of six changes to his starting lineup from the XI that began the 1-0 loss to Ipswich Town before the international break, including a landmark start in attack for Luca Williams-Barnett.

The 18-year-old makes his full Premier League debut at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as part of a much-changed attack, which also sees Dominic Solanke and James Maddison replace Omar Marmoush and Archie Gray.

Further back, Destiny Udogie and Marcos Senesi have displaced Andy Robertson and Micky van de Ven, who are on the bench alongside Marmoush, Gray and the returning Savio and Lucas Bergvall.

Tonali has played over 500 more Premier League minutes than Gallagher so far this season, but the England international nevertheless leads his Italian colleague in several per 90 metrics.

As per the comparison chart, Gallagher ranks higher in terms of duels won, tackles and interceptions per 90, as well as winning more free kicks and committing more fouls.

The former Chelsea man also attempts more shots per game and boasts a higher ratio of shots on target, but Tonali triumphs in terms of successful passes, substantial chances created and dribble success rate.

However, with a fully-fit Maddison back in the starting lineup, Spurs should have little in the way of creativity concerns as De Zerbi's men bid to return to winning ways on home territory.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Exact recovery times will only be set once all clinical tests are complete.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Defenders Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo hurt their hamstrings at Napoli, leaving unbeaten Serie A leaders Lazio short in defence. The setback hits Gattuso's back line just as Juventus return from the break chasing the leaders.

Lazio’s defence has suffered a double blow. Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo were both injured in the 1-1 draw at Napoli. The timing is awkward for the leaders, who resume their league campaign against Lecce on 21 November.

Exact recovery times will only be set once all clinical tests are complete. The early estimate is about 20 days for each player, Sky Sport Italia reported. On that timeline, both miss the home game against Lecce and could return for the trip to Torino on 28 November.

It has been revealed that not every report is that hopeful. Football Italia reported that the pair should miss both the Lecce and Torino games. Under that scenario, they hope to be available again in the first week of December. The match against Atalanta on 6 December is also in doubt.

Tavares has been a real attacking outlet this season. He has one goal and four assists in 11 Serie A games. He also has a long record of muscle injuries. Sutalo has made eight league appearances since joining on loan from Ajax on 22 August.

Lazio must now turn to their alternatives. Alfonso Pedraza, who joined from Villarreal in the summer, is the leading option at left-back. He has played 322 minutes across the league and Coppa Italia. Diogo Leite and Doekhi are competing to replace Sutalo in the middle.

The stand-ins inherit a strong record. Lazio have scored 25 goals and conceded 9 so far. Keeping that defensive record with a reshuffled back line is now Gattuso’s task.

Sources indicate that juventus know Lazio’s quality first-hand. Gattuso’s side won 3-0 in Turin earlier this season. That result still weighs on the table. Five wins, three draws and three defeats make up the Juventus record from their opening games.

Grande chiusura di Sutalo, fondamentale.

— S.S.Lazio (@OfficialSSLazio) November 8, 2026.

Sources indicate that two missing defenders will not close the gap on their own. They do, however, give Juventus a window in which the leaders are weaker than usual. Any dropped points by Lazio over the coming rounds would only count if Juventus take care of their own fixtures.

Those fixtures follow Lazio’s closely. Como v Juventus is scheduled for Sunday 29 November at 20:45, the day after Lazio’s game against Torino. Further ahead, Lazio’s aim is to have both defenders fit for the Rome derby on 13 December.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026.

The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.

United suffered the embarrassing security breach on Pochettino’s first day as head coach after the 12-minute footage showing the Argentine and his staff working with the players at Carrington was posted online.

The owner of the account called CC Overview, who is known only as Colin, justified the intrusion by saying that the airspace over Carrington is unrestricted and the drone was operating legally within Civil Aviation Authority rules.

United will have to apply to the Department of Transport if they want to close off the airspace to avoid more unwanted drones.

CC Overview took the video down on Friday morning insisting that he was unaware of the significance of his actions.

He also clarified that neither Liverpool – who are United’s opponents in Pochettino’s first game at Anfield on Sunday – nor any other club were involved in the filming.

Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session was filmed by a drone and the operator has now apologised.

The drone user, who is known only as Colin, noted he had not broken laws but apologised.

United have declined to comment over the incident and it’s unclear if the club have made contact with him or involved Greater Manchester Police.

Recent findings suggest that his statement read: ‘I would like to speak about yesterday’s incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.

‘My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time.

'I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

‘I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets.

'I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match. I would also like to state that Liverpool Football club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday.

It has been revealed that ‘The video has been removed from my channel. I have spent the past four years building up my YouTube channel and were well regarded in the fields I film and would now like to get back to building up my damaged reputation and making well received responsible videos. Thank you.’.

United say they will not pursue legal action this time but will not hesitate to do so if it happens in the future.

To stop drones legally flying over Carrington, it has emerged that the club would need to seek permission from the Government to restrict the airspace around the training ground.

Footage of the session was captured close to Carrington and uploaded online.

Sources indicate that there are tight controls issued by the CAA and National Air Traffic Services over flying drones of different sizes, and a code of conduct related to how they are operated. It includes sharing photos and videos that could be ‘unfair’ to anyone.

It states that drones over 250g should not be flown closer than 50 metres to people, and drones below that weight should not be flown over crowds.

In a recent development, the drone and model aircraft code also states that you must ‘keep at least 150m away from residential, recreational, commercial and industrial areas’. It lists sports facilities as a recreational area.

There are also rules regarding privacy, which may well apply to United given that Pochettino and his players were preparing for a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday – arguably the biggest fixture in the English football calendar.

Recent findings suggest that it states: ‘Drones consumers must always respect your privacy and not cause a nuisance. They must comply with the same privacy regulations as anyone who uses a camera or recording device.

Man United installed signs in 2018 warning that the use of drones over Carrington was 'strictly prohibited' and would be reported for prosecution.

‘If your drone or model aircraft is fitted with a camera or listening device, you must respect other people’s privacy whenever you use them. If you use these devices where people can expect privacy, such as inside their home or garden, you’re likely to be breaking data protection laws. Any photos or recordings you take may be covered by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

Industry observers note that ‘Let people know before you start recording or taking pictures. In some cases, this will be easy. For example, if you’re taking a photo of family and friends at a family barbecue. In other cases, this will be less practical, so you must be careful to respect everyone’s right to privacy.

Sources indicate that ‘Think before sharing photos and videos. Avoid sharing anything that could be unfair or harmful to anyone. Think carefully about who could see your photos and videos – especially before posting them on social media. Apply the same common-sense approach that you would with images or video recorded on a smartphone or digital camera.’.

According to recent reports, liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was asked about the drone on Friday, saying: 'It shouldn't be legal. There is a reason why we train behind closed doors. It's not nice for any club.'.

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he mentioned with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

In a recent development, the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

It has been revealed that if you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had mentioned he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Recent findings suggest that “He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

It is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

Industry observers note that they travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

According to recent reports, “You don’t have a lot of time to train,” mentioned Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are at the moment third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Two of the Premier League's most successful clubs renew their fierce rivalry on Sunday as Liverpool welcome Manchester United to Anfield for their first meeting of the season.

The Reds are navigating a period of transition under Andoni Iraola, but have made an encouraging start to the campaign, climbing to fourth in the Premier League table with 18 points.

Manchester United, meanwhile, have endured their worst start to a new season, prompting the club hierarchy to part ways with Michael Carrick, who guided them into the Champions League places last term.

The Red Devils have wasted little time in appointing Mauricio Pochettino as his successor, but the Argentine faces a daunting introduction to the rivalry, having won just three of his 19 managerial meetings with Liverpool.

Here, Sports Mole provides everything you need to know about how to tune into the contest.

Liverpool vs Man Utd is one of two Premier League fixtures scheduled for Sunday, with the other seeing Hull City welcome Brighton & Hove Albion.

The eagerly anticipated clash at Anfield is scheduled to get underway at 4.30pm UK time, a prime Sunday afternoon slot that should allow supporters both in the stands and watching from around the world to savour one of English football's biggest rivalries.

Liverpool vs Man Utd will take place at Anfield, the 61,276-capacity stadium that has served as the spiritual home of the mighty Reds since 1892.

Anfield is the fifth-largest football stadium in England and has been the setting for countless memorable encounters between these fierce rivals, with its famous atmosphere often adding another layer of intensity.

Beyond football, the iconic venue also opens its doors to major musical events during the off-season, with global superstar Taylor Swift among the big-name artists to have performed there during her record-breaking Eras Tour.

Non-Sky customers can stream the contest through a NOW Day or cancel-anytime Month pass, while viewers in India can catch the action live on JioHotstar.

Liverpool and Man Utd's official X accounts are expected to share match snippets throughout the contest, while journalists covering the game may also post their own footage and updates.

After the final whistle, extended highlights should be available on both clubs' official YouTube channels, while viewers in the UK can catch the action again on BBC's Match of the Day 2.

Liverpool have an opportunity to cut the gap to Manchester City to just one point with victory on Sunday, giving them an added incentive to make home advantage count.

The Reds have endured an uncomfortable run against their fiercest rivals at Anfield, having failed to beat the Red Devils on home soil since their emphatic 7-0 triumph in March 2023, and Iraola will be desperate to put that unwanted sequence behind them by claiming all three points.

The likes of Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz will be eager to rise to the occasion and deliver on a stage of such magnitude, but Liverpool's overriding priority is to turn their home performances into consistent results and strengthen their position in the title race.

For Man Utd, the stakes are arguably even higher, with the visitors desperate to climb out of the relegation zone and give their troubled campaign some much-needed impetus.

Pochettino, meanwhile, will be keen to mark the beginning of his Man Utd tenure with a statement victory, although he could hardly have been handed a more demanding opening assignment; given the circumstances, even a hard-earned draw at Anfield would represent a respectable start to his reign.

The Rossoneri have mustered a mere 126 shots so far, while Frosinone are quite far ahead at 221. On the flip side, the newly-promoted side have only scored one more goal than Milan (24 vs. 23), which is what makes this game so interesting.

Sources indicate that amorim has made it clear from the start that he wants to dominate each game. That shows in the possession, as Milan are third in Serie A with an average of 59% so far, and they also rank high in terms of passes per game.

Industry observers note that the shots are where they fall short, even if they average over two goals per game. There are several reasons for this, but most of it can be attributed to Amorim’s recent arrival and the fact that he has experimented rather extensively.

During today’s presser, he even said that they haven’t done anywhere near enough to enter the penalty box more often, which tends to mean more shots.

In a recent development, in the build-up, for example, the Rossoneri move the ball forward at an average speed of 1.30 meters per second, which is the slowest in Serie A. Alvini’s Frosinone, on the other hand, are great at vertical football: the ball moves toward the opponent’s penalty box at 2.51 meters per second, the best rate in the league.

Industry observers note that the Ciociari are masters of rapid counterattacks, so much so that on only 40 occasions have they built plays with ten or more passes. Milan, meanwhile, have 203.

It has been revealed that everything starts in the defence phase for Frosinone. Indeed, they always attempt to win the ball back inside the opponent’s half, which is proven by the index that measures the intensity of pressing in the attacking zone (they are first in Serie A).

It has been revealed that milan? They are eighth, despite being – along with Como – the team to have scored the most goals (4) from a ball recovered while pressing.

The difference between the two is well explained by the so-called “pressed sequences”, that is, the number of actions in open play in which a team manages to interrupt the opponent’s build-up within three passes or less, before the ball goes beyond the halfway line.

On that front, Frosinone are also first (161), while Milan are only 15th (102). Having mentioned all of this, as the pink newspaper concludes, we should expect a spectacular match tomorrow. Both teams will stick to their respective game, which bodes well.

#83584. Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

Manchester United could be forced to strengthen their attacking options in January after another injury setback involving Benjamin Sesko.

With Michael Carrick needing additional firepower to maintain competition for places up front, an experienced Premier League striker has reportedly emerged as a surprise target.

Recent findings suggest that leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin is among the names being considered by United’s recruitment team. However, attempting to sign a key player from one of their biggest rivals could prove extremely difficult.

According to The Athletic, Manchester United are exploring the January market for centre-forwards, with Calvert-Lewin one of the players under consideration.

The 29-year-old England international has reportedly been on United’s radar for some time, and recruitment staff are now assessing whether a potential transfer would be feasible when the window opens.

According to recent reports, the interest comes amid concerns over Benjamin Sesko’s availability. The Slovenian striker is expected to miss an extended period with a shin injury, leaving Carrick with fewer recognised centre-forward options.

According to recent reports, calvert-Lewin has rebuilt his career since joining Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in 2025. His performances at Elland Road have attracted renewed attention, with the striker scoring 20 goals in 49 appearances for the club across all competitions.

He has also returned to England international contention following his improved form, making him an appealing option for United as they consider their attacking requirements.

In a recent development, however, there are significant obstacles. Leeds are reportedly keen to reward Calvert-Lewin with a new contract, despite his current agreement running until 2028. The club are also understood to be protective of a player who has become an key part of Daniel Farke’s side.

The rivalry between Leeds and Manchester United presents another major complication. A transfer between the clubs would attract considerable attention, and reports suggest the possibility of an agreement is at the moment remote.

According to recent reports, calvert-Lewin could offer United a different profile in attack, bringing physical presence, aerial ability and considerable Premier League experience. His availability could become particularly notable if Sesko remains sidelined into the January window.

United have previously considered alternative centre-forward options, but the latest developments could encourage the recruitment department to widen its search. Calvert-Lewin’s experience in English football would potentially make him an attractive short-term solution.

Nevertheless, Leeds are unlikely to make negotiations straightforward. They have little reason to weaken their squad midway through the campaign, particularly by allowing an notable player to join their historic rivals.

United must also consider whether pursuing Calvert-Lewin is realistic when other striker targets may be easier to acquire.

It has been revealed that for now, the reported interest represents an option under consideration rather than an imminent transfer. Sesko’s injury has increased the urgency surrounding United’s search for attacking reinforcements, but persuading Leeds to sell their striker could prove a significant challenge.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:07 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 20 November 2026.

Manchester United have fallen victim to a security breach after footage of Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session as head coach was leaked online.

The 12-minute video taken by a drone hovering over the club’s Carrington training complex on Thursday clearly indicates Pochettino and his coaching staff working with the players.

United have refused to comment.

The incident is a major embarrassment for United on Pochettino’s first full day in charge after the club paid £10million to buy the Argentine and his staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

His first game is against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, although it’s unclear how much United’s bitter rivals would be able to benefit from the video.

United regularly use their own drones to film training sessions, but put up signs six years ago banning the use of them near the training ground in case they could reveal top-secret information to their opponents.

Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session has been leaked on YouTube.

Footage of the session was captured from a drone close to Carrington and uploaded online.

Man United players were captured during a drill under the gaze of Pochettino's coaching staff.

The footage was posted on YouTube by an account called CC Overview which insists that the airspace over Carrington is unrestricted and the drone was operating legally within Civil Aviation Authority rules.

It said that the video was taken half an hour into Pochettino’s training session and clearly indicates the 54-year-old instructing the United squad along with his coaching team of No.2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya.

Pochettino only flew into Manchester on Wednesday with D’Agostino, Tuya and analyst Alec Scott after taking charge of his last game as US coach against Haiti in Cincinnati.

They caught a private jet provided by United after the game and he went straight to Carrington after landing in the UK shortly before noon.

Perez, Jimenez and Sebastiano Pochettino have been at the training ground since the weekend after being given permission by the US Soccer Federation to leave after the first-leg against Haiti in Miami.

Pochettino addressed the Man United's internal media team for the first time on Thursday, outlining how he plans to drag this underperforming squad up the table.

'The culture is the most key,' Pochettino explained.

'Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

The breach comes as Man United prepare for a daunting trip to Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

The 12 minutes of drone footage captured Pochettino and his staff coaching across two training pitches at Carrington.

Man United installed signs in 2018 warning that the use of drones over Carrington was 'strictly prohibited' and would be reported for prosecution.

'We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.'.

Recent findings suggest that 'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure.'.

Pochettino has stressed he is focused on the potential of his squad, rather than their present position in the Premier League.

'It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,' a defiant Pochettino added.

'Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most notable thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure [off].

'Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

'When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

'That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

'I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 15:24, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 15:43.

Chelsea have been dealt yet another injury blow concerning Moises Caicedo, who was forced off in the first half of Saturday's Premier League clash with Leeds United.

The 25-year-old was making his sixth start of the top-flight season at Stamford Bridge, joining Romeo Lavia in the centre of the park, but his race was run with just 22 minutes gone.

Caicedo was involved in a heavy mid-air collision with James Justin early doors and was left in a heap on the ground, but he was ultimately able to carry on, albeit briefly.

The Ecuador international sat down on the turf just moments later and covered his face with his arm as he was attended to by medical staff, before hobbling off the field to be replaced by Jordan Henderson.

Caicedo appeared to be struggling with a back injury and was given an ice pack as he sat down on the bench, shortly before the Blues took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha.

The severity of Caicedo's latest concern is yet to be ascertained, and it may well be that the South American simply sustained a contact injury which will heal in a matter of days.

However, the midfielder's withdrawal prolonged a painful stop-start season, in which he has already missed six games across the Premier League and EFL Cup due to two separate injuries.

Caicedo sat out Chelsea's opening two games vs. Fulham and Luton Town owing to a knock, before picking up a calf problem just 14 minutes into his first appearance of the campaign against Brighton & Hove Albion.

The Blues faced Leeds (in the EFL Cup), Arsenal, Hull City and Brentford without Caicedo due to his new calf problem, since when he has been a mainstay in Alonso's midfield with the captain's armband.

The Ecuadorian is now an early doubt for next Friday's trip to Nottingham Forest, though, as well as Chelsea's London derby at home to Crystal Palace on December 2.

Caicedo's fitness struggles in the 2026-27 season are uncharacteristic, as the 25-year-old missed just two games through injury or illness in his first three campaigns at the club.

Both of those absences occurred in his debut 2023-24 campaign, in which he missed a 0-0 draw with Bournemouth because of a knock, and a 2-1 defeat to Wolverhampton Wanderers due to illness.

Caicedo navigated the entire 2024-25 season without picking up an injury, starting all 38 Premier League games and being omitted from several Conference League squads to enjoy a well-earned rest.

The midfielder then made another 50 appearances in the 2025-26 season, and his only notable absences were due to suspension rather than fitness problems.

Alonso is already missing Joao Pedro, Jamie Gittens, Maxence Lacroix, Jorrel Hato and Reece James, and none is expected to return before the end of the month.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino.
  • Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches.
  • Recent findings suggest that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

Recent findings suggest that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

According to recent reports, the trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

Industry observers note that the contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Sources indicate that luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Industry observers note that close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

Industry observers note that the run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

After Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has mentioned he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. A few hours before the clash between Italy and France, this Thursday (8:45 p.m.) in the League of Nations, the former Italian defender returned to the famous headbutt received in the chest, drawing a parallel with the recent death of Jesus de Miguel. A tragedy which pushed Materazzi to wonder about the consequences that Zidane’s gesture in 2006 could have had. The death of Jesus de Miguel made me thank God that nothing serious happened. Last October, the former number 10 of the Blues returned to this episode by admitting that he was not proud of his gesture, without directly apologizing to his former opponent.

A position that Marco Materazzi continues to regret. “ In his place, I would have said: “I made a mistake, but I was provoked. The Italian world champion also recounted an unexpected meeting with Zidane in November 2010, in Milan, on the eve of a match between AC Milan and Real Madrid. According to his account, he spontaneously went to shake hands with the Frenchman, who replied: “ Don’t worry, these things happen, it’s in the past. » Materazzi, however, regrets that Zidane then claimed to have taken him for a simple supporter. Despite this persistent dispute, the Italian does not hide his admiration for the coaching qualities of the former playmaker. I like everything about his approach. He knows the players, understands the champions, gives them space and creates empathy. It’s fundamental to winning “, he stressed. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside.
  • Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April.
  • TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside. The report claims an offer of around £80m could change that stance, although Villa negotiate from strength because the 26-year-old’s contract runs until 2030.

January looks highly unlikely. Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April. Unai Emery cannot lose a second holding midfielder in the middle of a season. The summer is different. CaughtOffside states Villa could entertain a significant bid then, provided they can reinvest the money in a proper replacement and strengthen the squad around him.

TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why. Kamara has started all 10 of his Premier League games this season, completing 86.3% of his passes, including 83 line-breaking balls, while making 28 tackles and 40 recoveries. He wins 56% of his duels and can play at centre-back, which would give Mikel Arteta cover in two positions.

In a recent development, the weaknesses are just as clear. He has no goals this season, only three shots and an xG of 0.14, and he has committed 20 fouls and conceded a penalty. He also missed the closing weeks of 2024/25 through injury.

Sources indicate that the role he would play is obvious: a ball-playing six next to Declan Rice. Martín Zubimendi occupies it now, and Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, six clear of Manchester City, with seven clean sheets.

In a recent development, no, not at that price. Arsenal spent £75m on Bruno Guimarães in August, and Arteta still has Rice, Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly competing for the same central spaces.

Recent findings suggest that fotMob values him at €49m, roughly £43m, so Villa would be asking close to double his market value for a player who turns 27 this month and offers little in the final third. Villa’s insistence on reinvesting the fee also hands them the leverage, which means Arsenal would pay a premium on a seller’s timetable.

It has been revealed that the only sensible trigger is a departure, perhaps Zubimendi or the 30-year-old Merino, leaving Arsenal short of a proven Premier League six. Kamara is a better holding midfielder than most of the market, but a title-leading side already has that job covered, and £80m would buy cover rather than improvement.

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

Industry observers note that frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

Industry observers note that they are at the moment on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

Sources indicate that while collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly substantial-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met.
  • It has been revealed that the numbers explain the concern.
  • Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

It has been revealed that the numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

According to recent reports, chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

According to recent reports, fotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

Recent findings suggest that A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October. With Pierre Kalulu already sidelined, Juventus face tests that could leave them without both main right-sided defenders for Venezia and Omonia.

Sources indicate that zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. His left hamstring tightened up as he went through the warm-up. He was taken out of the matchday squad as a precaution. Barış Alper Yılmaz started in his place.

An Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

Industry observers note that çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

The location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

Tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Recent findings suggest that çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

Juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

According to recent reports, if Çelik’s problem proves to be a relapse, Spalletti could be without both of his main right-sided defenders for those two games. The schedule offers little room for recovery. The Omonia match is the second of four games in 12 days.

The league position adds pressure. After 11 rounds Juventus are seventh in Serie A with 18 points. Their record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats.

Sources indicate that venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

Published: 15:33 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 20 November 2026.

Rangers goalkeeper Ivor Pandur has revealed his 'unbelievable' experience of working under Allan McGregor.

The former Rangers, Hull and Scotland keeper was brought into the Ibrox backroom staff by Derek McInnes as lead goalkeeping coach in the summer.

Pandur is reaping the benefits of his mentor’s experience and their relationship having kept eight clean sheets during his team’s 12-match unbeaten run.

'It’s unbelievable,' said the Croatian ahead of the Premiership encounter at Motherwell on Saturday night.

'With the career that he had here, he obviously has a lot of experience.

In a recent development, 'We have a great relationship where he is my coach, he is my friend. So he’ll tell me when I ask him if I can do something better.

Ivor Pandur has made an impressive start to life at Rangers after joining from Hull City.

'We are here to make each other better. If I can make him a better coach, that’s brilliant. But he’s making me a better goalkeeper and I’m really, really thankful for that.

'Training, first of all, is really, really enjoyable. And he always asks, "What do I want to do? What do I want to improve?". And he’ll give me feedback.

'There’s not a single thing, I would say, that made me better. Just in general, to be able to work in these kind of circumstances and conditions, it’s really enjoyable and it’s making me happy every day.

'It’s making me excited to come to work. And that’s because of him also.

'He’s a great guy and he was a great goalkeeper, and it’s enough for me to learn from.'.

Manager McInnes this week described Pandur as a key 'driver' of team culture off the pitch, citing the respect he has from his team-mates.

Pandur, who joined from Hull in the summer, remarked: 'I always want to lead by example. The words are not so key if you’re not doing your job right.

'So if I can lead by example and show up every day, work as hard as I can, a lot of young players can see that.

Pandur insists he is only going to keep improving under the guidance of Allan McGregor.

'And obviously, I’m always there to help somebody. I was also 19 or 20 and, when I had somebody to learn from, it was much easier.

'Because you get experiences through life and through years of playing, I always try to help everybody else.

'So there are times where I can be more vocal if I feel a need for it, but it’s never my first objective. It’s always to lead by example.'.

Pandur is still awaiting his first international cap but was again away with Croatia this month and he feels meeting the demands of Rangers fans is getting the best out of him.

'It keeps you on your toes,” the former Rijeka, Hellas Verona and Fortuna Sittard player remarked. 'But in my opinion, pressure is in your head.

Sources indicate that 'We all play the game we love and we try to do our best. Some days you’ll do good, some days you’ll do bad. We always try to do the right thing.

According to recent reports, 'Pressure is bigger here, there’s more followers. But it can only make you better because it gets everything out of you.'.

Liverpool sit fourth.

It has been revealed that yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Recent findings suggest that iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Tottenham Hotspur youngster Luca Williams-Barnett repaid Roberto De Zerbi's faith in him with a goal and assist in Saturday's 2-0 Premier League victory over Ipswich Town.
  • The 18-year-old was handed his first Premier League start against the Tractor Boys in place of the injured Mathys Tel, having shown glimpses of his potential off the bench against Leeds United and Crystal Palace.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 17:00, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 17:08.

Tottenham Hotspur youngster Luca Williams-Barnett repaid Roberto De Zerbi's faith in him with a goal and assist in Saturday's 2-0 Premier League victory over Ipswich Town.

The 18-year-old was handed his first Premier League start against the Tractor Boys in place of the injured Mathys Tel, having shown glimpses of his potential off the bench against Leeds United and Crystal Palace.

With 15 minutes gone at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Williams-Barnett muscled his way beyond Abdoul Ouattara to meet Pedro Porro's cross and bundle the ball into the back of the net for the opening goal.

The 2008-born youngster followed up his maiden Premier League goal with a fine assist in the second period, driving down the left-hand side and crossing for Dominic Solanke to crash home.

Williams-Barnett made way for Savio in the 64th minute, having been booked shortly after Solanke's goal, but not without becoming Tottenham's third-youngest Premier League scorer ever.

At 18 years, one month and 20 days old, Williams-Barnett is only older than Andy Turner and Gareth Bale when they scored their first Premier League goals for Tottenham.

Turner holds the club record, having scored at just 17 years and five months against Everton in 1992, while Bale was just four days younger than Williams-Barnett is now when he netted against Fulham in September 2007.

Furthermore, Williams-Barnett has overtaken Tottenham traitor Sol Campbell on the list, as the latter was 18 years and two months old when he scored his maiden Spurs Premier League goal.

Aaron Lennon, Reto Ziegler and Dele Alli are the only other players in the top 10 to have scored their first Tottenham Premier League goals in the 2000s.

While Williams-Barnett stole the spotlight at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the teenager did not quite manage to break either a club or Premier League record.

Despite both scoring and setting up a goal in North London, Williams-Barnett is only the second-youngest player to both score and assist in a Premier League game, behind Michael Owen.

The former Ballon d'Or winner was just 17 years and 364 days old when he scored and assisted for Liverpool against Crystal Palace in 1997, before also doing so against Leeds United at 18 years and 12 days.

Nevertheless, Williams-Barnett has made his case to also start next Sunday's clash away to Sunderland, as well as the first North London derby of the season on December 6.

Spurs' victory over Ipswich has lifted De Zerbi's side up to ninth in the Premier League table on 15 points from 11 matches, just three points worse off than fourth-placed Bournemouth.

Breaking: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3438 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open latest opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8,9,10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

In a recent development, a, Detailed device schematic. A niobium film is patterned on a 500 μm thick 171Yb3+:YVO4 crystal. A 100 nm gold layer is evaporated on the back side, forming a weak optical Fabry-Pérot mode between the front and back chip reflections. b, Calibration of spin-cavity coupling strength. By optically pumping the population into the \(| \downarrow \rangle \) state, we probe the resonant spin-cavity coupling spectrum and its strength while avoiding superradiant effects. The blue data in the bottom subpanel correspond to the continuous-wave (CW) pump being off, while the black data are taken with a 400 μW continuous-wave pump. By fitting to a spin-cavity coupling model, we extract an ensemble coupling strength of \(\sqrt{N}g\approx 2\pi \times 1.1\) MHz, corresponding to a normalized coupling gnorm ≈ 0.6 < 1. The single-spin coupling, g = 2π × 10 Hz, and the effective ensemble size, N = 1010, are estimated from Comsol simulation and dopant concentration. c, Ensemble coupling strength, \(\sqrt{N}g\), as a function of pump power. We observe that the ensemble coupling strength increases with pump power, indicating a larger population in the microwave spin manifold.

It has been revealed that a, A pulsed, transient optical pumping scheme that drives 171Yb3+ spins into the \(| \uparrow \rangle \) state. The resulting inverted spin polarization is resonantly coupled to a microwave cavity, leading to a superradiant burst in the microwave domain. b, Example of a delayed superradiant burst. A 1 mW pump is applied for 50 μs, after which a microwave superradiant burst is observed with a delay time τd. The superradiant signal is normalized by its peak-to-peak amplitude. c and d, Burst delay times, τd, and burst width, τw, measured as a function of the optical pump detuning, Δpump, which controls the optical transition strength from \(| g\rangle \) to \(| \uparrow \rangle \). A symmetric dependence of τd and τw is observed, with shorter delay times and narrower widths near resonance. This behaviour is consistent with the expected scaling τd, τw ∝ 1/N, as the pump detuning effectively controls the ensemble size, N, in the microwave spin manifold. Data points represent mean values, with error bars indicating the standard deviation over 300 repeated measurements.

It has been revealed that a, Frequency-domain measurement of continuous-wave microwave superradiance, showing a much narrow linewidth of  ≈ 30 Hz. The inhomogeneously broadened ensemble line profile (dashed line) is overlaid for comparison. b, Dependence of the linewidth of continuous-wave superradiance on emission power, PMW. An inverse relationship between the linewidth and the emission power is observed, consistent with a noise-broadened Schawlow-Townes linewidth. The lower dashed line denotes the pump laser noise-limited bound. These results confirm that the disordered spin ensemble emits continuous-wave superradiance with a much narrower spectral linewidth. c, Continuous-wave superradiance emission frequency at different optical pump detunings. A linear correlation between the microwave emission frequency and optical pump detuning is observed, with a slope of  −1.23 kHz/MHz.

a, Four representative data traces under a 1 ms continuous optical pump. Random onset times of the emergent periodic pulsed phase are observed. b, Zoom-in of individual burst trains showing the distribution of burst onset times, {τk}, where k denotes the experimental repetition index. After an initial settling time, both the amplitudes, {Ak}, and the periodicity, T, become independent of k, indicating the establishment of a robust pulsed superradiance phase. c, Burst onset phases, defined as θk = 2π × τk/T (mod 2π), measured over 50 repetitions under identical experimental conditions. The phases are randomly distributed over 2π, demonstrating spontaneous breaking of continuous time-translation symmetry in the absence of any external timing reference.

a, Schematic of periodic pulsed superradiance, characterized by three parameters: the pulse-train periodicity T, the peak emission power Ppeak, and the average emission power \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\). b-d, show fits to the experimental data presented in Fig. 3 of the main text, where T, Ppeak, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\) exhibit good agreement with the expected scaling behaviours of T ∝ 1/N, Ppeak ∝ N2, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\propto {N}^{2}\), respectively. Here, N is the effective number of spins in the microwave manifold, tuned via the optical pump detuning, Δpump. When sweeping Δpump, the optical pump power is fixed, corresponding to an excitation over an optical inhomogeneity Γop = 2π × 92 MHz in all three cases.

a, Relative contributions of superradiance (blue) and stimulated emission (red) to the emission strength in the periodic superradiance phase. b, Comparison of emission patterns between the many-body case with N = 1010 atoms (blue) and the single-atom case with N = 1 (red). For a fair comparison, the total effective cavity coupling strength is fixed to \({g}_{{\rm{tot}}}=\sqrt{N}g=2\pi \times 1\,{\rm{MHz}}\) for both cases. c, Comparison of emission patterns in the presence (blue) and absence (red) of spin frequency inhomogeneity, i.e., disorder. All simulations are performed using experimental parameters corresponding to the periodic superradiance phase in Regime III.

a and b, show simultaneously recorded microwave periodic superradiance and transferred optical periodic superradiance, respectively, over a duration of up to 100 ms. c, Zoom-in windows near 1, 50, and 100 ms showing synchronized dual-rail emission patterns, maintaining persistent and robust pulse periodicity without decay.

According to recent reports, a, Microwave (blue) and optical (yellow) amplitudes, A(t), extracted from IQ detection as A(t) = ∣I(t) + iQ(t)∣. The I and Q signals, I(t) and Q(t), are measured continuously over 2 ms, capturing 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. The microwave and optical channels exhibit synchronized and reproducible temporal profiles. The grey shaded area indicates the noise floor determined from the optical signal, below which the phase extraction is not reliable. b, Normalized amplitude stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. τ denotes the peak emission time, identified for each burst from the time-domain pulse train. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical normalized amplitudes, which are 0.009 and 0.05, respectively. c, Time-domain phase profiles, \(\phi (t)={\tan }^{-1}[Q(t)/I(t)]\), extracted from IQ detection. The microwave and optical pulse trains exhibit synchronized and reproducible phase profiles over time. Phase values in regions dominated by the optical-signal noise floor are greyed out, where large fluctuations are observed. The chirping behaviour during each pulse qualitatively follows the amplitude profile, which can be attributed to an effective Kerr nonlinearity induced intensity dependence. d, Phase stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts, zoomed in on the region above the noise floor. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical phase values, which are 0.03π and 0.11π, respectively. See Methods for details.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Weston McKennie has stated USA players could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, days after his national team coach took the job there.
  • Industry observers note that the question put to Weston McKennie was whether USA players might follow their coach to Old Trafford.
  • McKennie called the speculation inevitable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Weston McKennie has stated USA players could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, days after his national team coach took the job there. Juventus, already without Thuram and Locatelli, now face pressure to rule out a mid-season sale.

Industry observers note that the question put to Weston McKennie was whether USA players might follow their coach to Old Trafford. His answer was that it could potentially happen.

McKennie called the speculation inevitable. He remarked many USA players are due to change clubs within the next year, calciomercato.com reported.

Industry observers note that pochettino was asked about the same subject. He stated now was not the right time to discuss it. He added that United are among the very top clubs and a dream for many players.

Sources indicate that pochettino and his staff remain in charge of the USA for two games against Haiti, on 14 and 17 November. United agreed with the federation that the staff would be released once those national-team duties were over. Pochettino became USA head coach in September 2024. His record with the national team stands at 21 wins, 12 defeats and two draws from 35 matches.

In a recent development, the comments land awkwardly in Turin. Reports had already linked United with a January move for the American. Juventus regard him as central to Luciano Spalletti’s aims and are reluctant to let him leave mid-season, ESPN reported.

His contract, which runs until June 2030, offers the club some protection. It was signed only months before Pochettino’s switch to English football.

McKennie arrived from Schalke 04 in August 2020. His value to Spalletti lies in his flexibility.

The club noted in its renewal announcement that he had been used on both flanks under Spalletti. He had also recently played as a striker.

The timing makes McKennie harder to replace. He is one of the few senior midfielders Spalletti still has available.

According to recent reports, thuram is out until 2027 after knee surgery. Captain Manuel Locatelli also faces a long absence after twisting his right knee against Milan. He had surgery in Lyon on 8 September to repair the external meniscus, and Corriere dello Sport put his lay-off at five to six months.

Losing him in January would thin the squad further at a delicate point of the season. Juventus are chasing a Champions League place. Qualification is key to the club’s finances.

That is why the club’s stance matters as much as the player’s words.

McKennie’s own answer was measured. He mentioned nobody knows which players a coach really wants.

For now, the pressure falls on Juventus. A clear statement ruling out a January sale would end the debate. Silence would leave it open until the window.

Industry observers note that the next step comes at Old Trafford. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United from 18 November, and his first squad decisions will show whether the interest is real.

If it’s a good fee and we can reinvest into two players to help the squad depth I would be fine with it.

  • A 1-0 win at the Houston Dynamo ensured St Louis finished third in the Western Conference MLS standings while Los Angeles wound up in sixth, losing 2-1 to the Seattle Sounders on Decision Day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 21 Nov 2026 18:37.

In search of their first MLS playoff victory, St Louis City will welcome Los Angeles FC to Energizer Park for game one of that best-of-three series on Monday.

A 1-0 win at the Houston Dynamo ensured St Louis finished third in the Western Conference MLS standings while Los Angeles wound up in sixth, losing 2-1 to the Seattle Sounders on Decision Day.

For the first time since their inaugural campaign in 2023, St Louis have made the post-season, finishing with 54 points in 2026.

Under Yoann Demet, this team earned 22 more points this year when compared to 2025 and were just two points short of equaling their best-ever campaign in 2023.

While they won nine regular-season affairs at Energizer Park this year, on Monday this team will try to snap a three-match MLS winless run at home, collecting just one point over that stretch.

St Louis have lost their only two playoff outings and have not been in front for a single second in any of those post-season fixtures.

During the regular season, they failed to lose a single league game at home when netting the opening goal, dropping points in only two of those instances.

In 2026, they had a perfect home record against the two LA clubs in MLS, holding on to a narrow 2-1 home win over LAFC in May.

Los Angeles FC were not satisfied with the direction they were heading in this fall, but their coaching change has made little difference.

Since Xavi Tamarit took over from Marc Dos Santos, the Black and Gold have claimed only one victory in league play and will try to avoid losing three straight matches to MLS teams on Monday for the second time this year.

Tamarit is still seeking his first domestic away triumph as the interim manager, while LAFC have not won an MLS away game since July against the Los Angeles Galaxy (3-0).

While they struggled on the road this season, the 2022 league champions have not lost in 90 minutes in their last two playoff outings as the visitors.

During the regular season, they conceded the second-fewest goals in the Western Conference (40) while averaging the third-fewest goals allowed per match in MLS (1.2).

The Black and Gold have earned points in seven of their eight all-time league meetings with St Louis City, including two wins and three clean sheets overall at Energizer Park.

St Louis City Major League Soccer form:.

St Louis City form (all competitions):.

Los Angeles FC Major League Soccer form:.

St Louis midfielder Carlo Holse is doubtful for game one due to a knee injury, Celio Pompeu is still recovering from a cruciate ligament tear, while Roman Burki will hope to return from concussion protocol.

Lukas MacNaughton had the only goal in their victory versus the Dynamo, and Ben Lundt made six stops to collect the clean sheet in place of Burki.

As for LAFC, Jacob Shaffelburg is unlikely to feature because of a rib fracture, Hugo Lloris is recovering from a rib injury of his own, Aaron Long has a head injury and Timothy Tillman is questionable due to a pelvic glitch.

Son Heung-min has scored in his last three playoff games, while Eddie Segura had the only goal in their Decision Day defeat against Seattle.

St Louis City possible starting lineup:.

Burki; MacNaughton, Baumgartl, Fall; Wallem, Polvara, Durkin, Totland; Downs, Navarro, Ostrak.

Los Angeles FC possible starting lineup:.

Carter; Hollingshead, Porteous, Segura, Cheberko; Choiniere, Delgado; Sieb, Walta, Bouanga; Heung-min.

Neither side were all that convincing down the stretch of the regular season, but the visitors have some proven performers who have stepped it up in knockout matches, and we believe that experience will give LAFC a narrow win in game one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It should have been an uneventful evening for FC Porto, who faced a Liga 3 team in the Portuguese Cup on Friday. But if the Dragoes avoided humiliation by qualifying on penalties (1-1, 3-1 tab), Francisco Moura will keep terrible memories of this meeting.

The 27-year-old defender scored one of the most incredible CSCs of the year. After a duel lost by Seko Fofana (who opened the scoring in the first period), and a ball pushed back by his goalkeeper, Francisco Moura pushed the leather into his own net, with a simple pass from the inside of his foot, very poorly assured.

According to recent reports, even if he was not really attacked, the former Famalicao player, with his back to goal, undoubtedly wanted to push the ball for a corner to avoid taking any risks. The least we can say is that he missed his gesture.

Immediately, his teammates and his goalkeeper came to comfort him. The FC Porto supporters, understanding, also applauded him.

In a recent development, “Anything can happen in the Cup, reacted coach Francesco Farioli on Sport TV. There have been several examples recently, it’s always difficult. Situations can arise that complicate everything. It’s part of football. As you saw, we are all behind Francisco (Moura). It’s unfortunate. The support from FC Porto players and even Paredes has been great, these are very positive gestures. ».
